name: Tatsumi
tagline: Tokyo in 19 minutes and Otemachi in 21 minutes. Served by 1 line. A one-room flat rents for roughly ¥110,000 to ¥120,000.
summary: The station is in Koto City, where Tokyo Metro run 1 line between them. Journey times to the main business districts are 21 minutes to Otemachi, 33 minutes to Shinjuku, 32 minutes to Shibuya and 30 minutes to Shinagawa. A one-room flat rents for roughly ¥110,000 to ¥120,000. The station stands 7 m above sea level, and the ground within 800 m varies in height by 4.9 m. The land around the station is close to level.

terrain.note: The station sits on the higher side of the ground around it, at 7 m above sea level. Within 800 m the ground ranges from 2.6 m to 7.5 m, a difference of 4.9 m.

hazards: On the flood hazard map for the largest rainfall the government models, the station itself falls outside the projected inundation area. Even so, 4 of the nine points within 400 m fall inside the area, and the deepest projection there is 0.5 to 3 m. For storm surge, 4 of the nine points also fall inside the projected area. On the whole, the flood projection here is on the small side for the 23 wards.
medical: Within an 800 m walk of the station there are 3 clinics and 1 pharmacy. The nearest hospital is 昭和医科大学江東豊洲病院, about 23 minutes' walk from the station. The next nearest is 鈴木リハビリテーション病院, about 24 minutes' walk. "Hospital" here means a facility OpenStreetMap records as one. OpenStreetMap does not record whether a facility admits inpatients or which departments it runs, so check each one on its own website. For which clinics open at night and at weekends, ask the emergency advice line of the ward you live in.
stationNote: 1 line serve the station: Tokyo Metro Yurakucho Line.
congestion: Tokyo Metro Yurakucho Line runs at 153% of capacity in the morning peak. The busiest stretch is 東池袋→護国寺, which this station is not on. At 150%, the ministry's scale describes shoulders not quite touching, with crowding near the doors. The figures describe each line's busiest stretch, so the stretch you ride may be easier.

rentRange.note: Around this station, One room ¥110,000 to ¥120,000 and 1K ¥120,000 to ¥130,000. 1LDK ¥200,000 to ¥210,000 and 2LDK ¥260,000 to ¥270,000. These are the per-station averages published by LIFULL HOME'S, Yahoo! Real Estate and at home, averaged together and rounded down to the nearest ¥10,000 (our own survey). All three are asking rents, so what tenants finally agree can be lower. Within the same station area the figure moves a great deal with the age of the building, the walk from the station, and whether the flat faces a main road.

rentReason: A one-room flat here goes for ¥110,000 to ¥120,000. Set against how long it takes to reach the central business districts, that is on the high side. quiet surroundings pushes the figure up. On the other side, only one line, the {line}, serving the station and little daily shopping within walking distance holds it down. For 2LDK, though, the sources differ by ¥30,000 or more. They count different sets of properties, so read those figures as a range rather than a point.

neighbours.lead: Tatsumi is ahead on how little of the area is in the flood projection and how close the centre is.
neighbours.note: Close enough to walk to from Tatsumi. Shinonome has the Rinkai Line, a different set from Tatsumi. To Toranomon, for instance, Shinonome takes 13 minutes longer. On safety, Tatsumi comes out ahead.

neighbours.lead: Shin-Kiba is ahead on the number of lines and how little of the area is in the flood projection, but Tatsumi is ahead on the number of medical facilities and quiet.
neighbours.note: About 1.5 km from Tatsumi in a straight line. Shin-Kiba also has the JR Keiyo Line and Rinkai Line, which Tatsumi does not. With more lines, Shin-Kiba is the better connected of the two. To Tokyo, for instance, Shin-Kiba is 7 minutes quicker. On quiet, though, Tatsumi comes out ahead.

goodFor: People who get around by bicycle or with a pushchair
notFor: People who want another route when service is suspended
People who want to finish their shopping on foot
People who want plenty of places to eat out
noiseSources: The 首都高速湾岸線 viaduct runs just outside the station. It is an expressway, so traffic is audible day and night
東京湾岸道路 (a main road) runs just outside the station. In a flat facing it, the cars are audible morning and evening

leads.terrain: The ground around the station is almost level, so you can choose where to live without thinking about slopes.
leads.groceries: There are 1 supermarkets within walking distance, and the nearest is 5 minutes on foot.
leads.hazards: The station itself is outside the projected flood area, but blocks nearby are inside it.
leads.stationNote: Only the Tokyo Metro Yurakucho Line serves this station, so when it stops you walk to another station.
leads.rentRange: Set against how long the commute takes, rents here are on the high side.
leads.medical: The number of clinics and pharmacies within walking distance is on the low side for the 23 wards.
leads.congestion: Morning loading on the lines here is about average for the 23 wards' stations.
leads.noiseSources: At this station, check the traffic noise before the noise people make.
